title: Symmetric fourth-moment criterion
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have the same distribution as $-X$, and suppose $X\in L^4(\mu)$. Assume its real-valued $L^2$ and $L^4$ norms satisfy $N_2(X)=1$ and $N_4(X)=C$ with $C>0$. For $0\le\rho<1$, $X$ is $(2,4,\rho)$-hypercontractive if and only if $\rho\le\min\{1/\sqrt3,1/C\}$.
replaced: Let $X\in L^4$ have a symmetric law on a probability space, $\|X\|_2=1$, and $\|X\|_4=C>0$. For $0\le\rho<1$, $H_{2,4,\rho}(X)$ holds if and only if $\rho\le\min(1/\sqrt3,1/C)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
